pr_title: statistics,domain: release statistics session periodically to avoid memory leak
pr_body:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to TiDB! Please read TiDB's [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/pingcap/community/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) document **BEFORE** filing this PR.
-->

### What problem does this PR solve? <!--add issue link with summary if exists-->

Fix https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/13883

Statistics worker goroutines use system session to execute SQL, that system session is never recycled. 
When executing a large transaction, statistic workers may come to work. After that some variables are referenced by the `sessionVars` in the system session and can't be released, leading to memory leaks.

### What is changed and how it works?

Refactor the `Handle` struct, extract the shared part out, provide `sessionctx.Context` for each worker goroutine.
In the `updateStatsWorker`, I'll recycle the session to avoid memory leak.

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

 - Manual test (add detailed scripts or steps below)
Run a large transaction and observe the memory footprint.

Code changes

 - Has exported function/method change
pr_comments:
> @tiancaiamao seems issue #13883 was fixed by #14031?

Yes.

I think it's safe to close this PR as long as the `SessionVar` of the pools' session don't hold too much memory.

issue_context.title: Memory leak after executing large transaction
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

1. What did you do?
If possible, provide a recipe for reproducing the error.

I'm testing the large transaction code in the master branch.
I find that after executing a large transaction, there is still quite a lot of memory used by TiDB.
Even I close the connection, the memory can't be released.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1420062/70064814-1929eb00-1625-11ea-9b49-ebe57b9d7260.png)

2. What did you expect to see?

TiDB should release all the memory after a large transaction finish.

3. What did you see instead?

Memory leak.

4. What version of TiDB are you using (`tidb-server -V` or run `select tidb_version();` on TiDB)?

master 093b27aea8ced42159b7c62d30dd9f811dd2c435
comments:
I'm not sure why but here is a suspicious place:

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/093b27aea8ced42159b7c62d30dd9f811dd2c435/statistics/handle/update.go#L401

I'll verify it tomorrow.

Yes, it's the leak!
The system session's `sessionVar` keeps `commitDetail`, and the `commitDetail` reference memory data from 2PC and so on.

review_comments: Do we need to mark it as in restricted sql?
Don't we need to put it back in pool?
